narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Child of epic #1589 **C3** (reserved Wave 3): turn `plan.policy.specGuard` / `verify:spec-drift` from **advise** into an **enforceable** gate.

PR #5315 ships Prefer-A Bound C1 + C2 (advise) and only the **C3 schema stub** (`sqaPass` engine no-op). Greptile holds #5315 below the 5/5 merge floor on fingerprints that require either a Bound-C2 recut or this C3 enforce work.

## Problem

In advise mode, agents can discharge drift coverage with stamps that Greptile treats as too soft:

1. **Impact declaration without rewrite proof** — `x-directive/specImpact` `delta|new` can satisfy advise discharge without proving the specification artifact was rewritten.
2. **Scope-level impact discharge** — any nested `delta|new` can clear the whole story; per-item uncovered siblings stay soft under the current Bound.

Those behaviors match locked Bound C2 (warn, do not hard-block). Enforce needs an explicit follow-up so #5315 is not thrashed as if they were accidental bugs.

## Scope (C3)

- Promote `specGuard` / `verify:spec-drift` from advise-default to an enforceable mode (exact policy surface TBD: `enforce` / `sqaPass` engine / merge-gate wiring).
- Require **proof of spec rewrite** (or an explicit human-origin disposition) when impact is claimed.
- Require **per-item** (or Bound-recut equivalent) impact coverage so nested stamps cannot silently clear uncovered siblings.
- Keep reconstruction (C1) draft-only; do not auto-promote specs as part of enforce.
- Document agents-entry / commands / CHANGELOG; wire fail-closed probe(s) the parent/CI can run.

## Non-goals

- Relitigating #5315 C1/C2 advise package as shipped.
- Auto-rewriting SPECIFICATION as a silent side effect of merge.
- Folding unrelated render/lifecycle adjacents (#630 / #1103 / #640) into this child.

## Evidence / refs

- Epic #1589 current-shape: C3 reserved (schema-validated, engine deferred) after C1/C2.
- PR #5315 Prefer-A Bound: C3 `sqaPass` schema-only / engine no-op.
- Greptile conf-hold fingerprints on #5315 (impact declaration bypasses coverage; item impacts miscounted) — intentional under Bound C2; actionable under this C3.

## Acceptance (draft)

- [ ] Typed policy + docs name how advise promotes to enforce (and what fails closed).
- [ ] Enforce path refuses impact discharge without rewrite proof or typed human disposition.
- [ ] Enforce path does not clear uncovered sibling items via a single nested stamp (or Bound documents the chosen coverage unit).
- [ ] Deterministic probe/tests cover advise-still-soft vs enforce-hard cases.
- [ ] agents-entry / commands / CHANGELOG updated; epic #1589 current-shape marks C3 in progress/done.

## Parent / standing

- Parent epic: #1589
- Blocks clean 5/5 merge of #5315 under standing Greptile floor unless floor-exception or Bound-C2 recut is chosen instead.

1. **Typed enforce promotion (P3).** Keep framework default advise. Document and implement how operators promote `plan.policy.specGuard.driftGuard.enforcement` to `enforce` (policy:show / policy write surface already typed). Recut `collectSpecImpacts` / `findingFromScopeCompletion` (or a parallel enforce evaluator) so soft whole-scope OR-aggregation is advise-only. Document the chosen coverage unit in agents-entry / commands.
4. **sqaPass posture (P3 adjacent).** Keep `sqaPass` schema; either leave engine no-op with documented escalate path, or land a minimal black-box fail path only if Bound names it as in-scope for this child. Do not silently fold #630 / #1103 / #640 render adjacents.
5. **Probes, docs, epic shape.** Deterministic tests cover advise-soft vs enforce-hard for rewrite-proof and per-item cases. Update agents-entry, commands, CHANGELOG, skill `deft-directive-spec-reconstruct`. Update epic #1589 current-shape when C3 lands. conflict_group suggestion: `spec-guard-enforce-c3`.
6. **Non-goals.** Relitigate #5315 C1/C2 advise package. Auto-rewrite SPECIFICATION as a merge side effect. Absorb unrelated render/lifecycle adjacents. Treat Greptile soft fingerprints on #5315 as accidental bugs rather than Bound-intentional advise behavior owned by this C3 leftover.

Round 1, fresh open critique of Prefer-A on Stop 1 (5995597071). Input ceiling: 5995617145. Verification: pin-read `git show 9e9054bac952d49edf2a563bb4dba67e3c3da096:`; source inspection, not executed fixtures. No sibling posts read.

Existing mechanisms checked before proposing changes: typed namespaced specGuard already validates advise/enforce and scope-complete/audit/both; evaluateSpecDrift already returns 0/1/2 and refuses invalid configuration, absent baseline, and absent ledger; the ledger holds baselineRevision plus unresolved scope rows; completion recursively OR-aggregates impacts; the existing specification sync is best-effort and post-move; sqaPass is explicitly no-op. Commands, agents-entry, and reconstruction skill preserve advise and draft-only reconstruction. These are extension points, not missing subsystems.

### 1. blocks-the-design — A changed baseline is not completion-specific rewrite proof

Evidence: at the pin, `packages/core/src/verify-source/spec-drift.ts`, requirementsFingerprint includes entire plan.items, while resolveBaselineRevision prefixes its fingerprint with xBRIEFInfo.updated. `scope/specification-sync.ts` runs registry synchronization before drift recording. The draft permits a changed requirements fingerprint OR baseline revision as evidence.

Failure: updating only the timestamp changes the baseline revision; lifecycle metadata inside an item can change the fingerprint. An unrelated requirements edit can also supply a changed fingerprint without covering the completing item. In concurrent work, one story's legitimate rewrite could otherwise be borrowed by another. This is a counterexample to the proposed proof criterion, not a demand for automated semantic judgment.

Disposition: the Bound cannot retain bare revision/fingerprint inequality as sufficient proof. Name a stable requirements-only projection and bind before/after evidence to the completing scope, item IDs, and affected requirement references. State explicitly that this proves a recorded relevant rewrite, not semantic correctness. Fixtures need timestamp-only, item-status/path-only, unrelated-requirement, and reused-evidence cases alongside a valid rewrite.

### 2. blocks-the-design — Per-item checking needs a durable denominator at promotion and audit

Evidence: `verify-source/spec-drift.ts` SpecDriftLedger stores only unresolved scope rows. recordScopeCompleteDriftAdvise deletes a whole scope's row after a delta/new declaration. evaluateSpecDrift returns clean when that ledger is empty and matches the current baseline; it does not revisit completed briefs. An audit-only trigger skips completion recording.

Failure: a ledger cleared under advise can remain empty at enforce promotion even though its completed items have no rewrite proof. Changing the completion collector cannot repair that missing history. Likewise, audit-only operation can miss a new uncovered completion against an unchanged specification. Within a scope, merely asking which items are 'shape-changing' leaves the coverage denominator undefined if missing declarations are allowed to exclude items.

Disposition: bind a specific enforce cutover/coverage boundary, stable item identities, and a deterministic rule for absent/invalid impacts and containers versus leaves. Either re-evaluate the eligible completed items at audit or retain sufficient validated coverage records; pre-enforce absence must be explicitly grandfathered at a recorded boundary or return unassessable, never silently count as proven. Test promotion from a matching empty advise ledger and audit-only uncovered completion, not only two siblings passed to the new collector. Reuse the existing ledger/audit surface rather than adding a separate policy authority.

### 3. blocks-the-design — The completion enforcement boundary must precede irreversible lifecycle success

Evidence: `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts` removes the source and updates lifecycle references before calling syncSpecificationAfterScopeMove; that function returns void and catches drift-recording exceptions. `spec-drift.ts` runSpecDriftCli already returns 1 for drift and 2 for unassessable even under advise. The draft currently leaves 'scope-complete refuse or durable block' and probe wiring open.

Failure: adding a hard finding to today's hook still permits completed lifecycle state, and a failed ledger write can leave no durable block. Calling the standalone probe fail-closed does not close this path unless a named consumer actually consumes both nonzero states. An enforced prerequisite with an unknown baseline must not look successful either.

Disposition: choose and name one executable boundary before bind. Prefer an enforce pre-move evaluation using the same evaluator, with post-move advise sync preserved. If choosing durable blocking instead, name its persisted state, write-failure behavior, and mandatory gate consumer. Cover exit 2 as well as exit 1, ledger write failure, and retry behavior. This does not require inserting advice into bare deft check or enabling sqaPass.

### 4. blocks-the-design — A typed 'human-origin' field does not establish human authority

Evidence: Stop 1 item 2 proposes a closed enum disposition stored on the completing brief; the pinned impact reader accepts values directly from that agent-editable JSON. The inspected specGuard/drift surfaces have no human-disposition origin verifier. This proposal introduces an authority-bearing bypass, so the untrusted-input lens applies.

Failure: the same agent whose rewrite is missing can write the allowed enum and claim human origin. Schema validation proves the token is valid, not that a human authorized the exception; copying an old disposition could also authorize a different item or revision.

Disposition: before binding this alternative, name the operator-authorized write/verification path and bind the disposition to scope, covered items, and revision/evidence context. Reuse an existing human-decision mechanism if it provides those guarantees; otherwise omit this alternative from the first ship. A freely editable origin label or reviewer attention is not the control. State the supported trust boundary rather than promising tamper-proofness against an actor with unrestricted repository access.

### 5. sharpens-framing — Preserve the actual compatibility and source boundaries

Evidence: the existing audit already has nonzero drift/config exits; enforce is already a valid typed value; `content/skills/deft-directive-spec-reconstruct/SKILL.md` declares its source as `packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json` and forbids direct edits. Epic [current shape, pass-3](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/1589#issuecomment-4753282449) records C1/C2 shipped via #5315, with C3 in #5350.

Failure: describing promotion as merely making the audit return nonzero obscures the missing evidence and lifecycle semantics; editing the rendered skill loses changes on regeneration; treating #5315 as still merge-blocked misstates the current work.

Disposition: the design can bind with corrected framing: preserve the audit's three-state interface, make enforce change evidence acceptance and named gate consumption, update the skill pack source plus generated artifact, and describe #5350 as the shipped advise package's enforce follow-up. Keep sqaPass no-op for this slice unless a separate concrete requirement justifies it.

Road not taken: a minimal global spec-hash change plus mandatory impact token is attractive because it is cheap and keeps SQA out of scope. It would be sufficient for a weaker 'some spec bytes changed' gate. It is insufficient for this draft's completion-specific and per-item claims; I would change that verdict if the Bound deliberately narrowed the promised guarantee and recorded the remaining pains as unresolved.

Plain take: the direction is sound, but the current draft can still certify a metadata edit, forget old uncovered work, complete a scope before blocking it, or accept an agent-written human exception. A bindable version needs precise evidence ownership and one real enforcement boundary. None of those requires automatic spec rewriting or a new SQA engine.

## Verdict

Prefer-A draft is the right C3 direction (typed enforce over advise soft discharge; keep C1 draft-only; keep sqaPass schema/no-op unless Bound names otherwise; non-goals match #1589 current-shape). It does **not** yet bind as written for P1/P2: rewrite-proof lacks a completion-scoped evidence seam against the live global baseline, and per-item coverage still offers an unbound "or equivalent" escape beside the live scope-level shapeChanging heuristic. P3 promote/fail-closed limbs need closed picks against the unread enforcement enum and the sync hook's advise catch-all.

## Inventory (existing mechanisms at pin)

- `plan.policy.specGuard.driftGuard.enforcement` is typed `advise|enforce`, default advise, validated in `validateSpecGuard` / `resolveSpecGuardFromTypedBlock` (`packages/core/src/policy/spec-guard.ts`). **Runtime readers do not branch on it.** `evaluateSpecDrift` never inspects enforcement; `recordScopeCompleteDriftAdvise` reads only `driftGuard.trigger`.
- Soft discharge lives in `findingFromScopeCompletion` + `collectSpecImpacts`: any nested `x-directive/specImpact` `delta|new` clears the whole scope (`packages/core/src/verify-source/spec-drift.ts`). Fixture `walks nested items/subItems for namespaced impact` expects `finding === null` under that OR.
- Shape-changing is **scope-level** today: tags/title regex OR `items.length > 0`. There is no per-item shape-changing predicate.
- Rewrite-adjacent evidence already exists as **project-global** `requirementsFingerprint` / `resolveBaselineRevision` on the specification artifact. Tests lock requirements content moves the baseline and status-only churn does not. Ledger (`spec-drift-ledger.json`) stores `baselineRevision` + unresolved findings with **no** per-completion pre/post fingerprint fields.
- Sync path: `syncSpecificationAfterScopeMove` (#2566) calls `recordScopeCompleteDriftAdvise` inside try/catch with explicit "advise path must not fail closed the lifecycle move" (`packages/core/src/scope/specification-sync.ts`).
- Inspect surface: `policy:show --field=specGuard` / `inspectSpecGuard`. `setPolicy` writes only `allowDirectCommitsToMaster` — no typed confirm verb for `specGuard.driftGuard.enforcement`.
- Human disposition adjacent: `pending-human-decisions.jsonl` (`packages/core/src/policy/decisions.ts`); `sqaPass` comment already says escalate may reuse it later. No brief-side closed disposition key for impact discharge today.
- Docs/skill at pin still describe C3 as schema-only / engine no-op (`deft-directive-spec-reconstruct` SKILL; agents-entry Spec reconstruction; commands near `verify:spec-drift`). ⊗ splice into bare `deft check` in v1 already recorded.
- Epic #1589 current-shape (comment 4753282449): Wave 3 = C3 via #5350; C1/C2 shipped under #5315 floor exception; adjacent #630/#1103/#640 not folded.

## Findings

### F1 — blocks-the-design: rewrite-proof "for that completion" has no completion-scoped seam

- **Evidence:** Prefer-A §2 requires fingerprint/baseline "changed for that completion". Live baseline is one global SPEC hash; ledger findings lack pre/post fields; scope-complete sync does not snapshot baseline before registry sync.
- **Failure mode:** Implement treats any global baseline move as proof for every concurrent completion (cross-story false clear), invents an unbound snapshot outside Bound, or collapses back to declaration-only under a "fingerprint moved sometime" gloss — P1 unrelieved.
- **Disposition consequence:** Prefer-A cannot bind §2 until it names the evidence artifact and comparison moment (e.g. ledger fields recording pre/post `baselineRevision` at the completing scopeId, or another Bound-named completion-scoped delta) relative to `syncSpecificationAfterScopeMove`.

### F2 — blocks-the-design: per-item coverage unit still unbound

- **Evidence:** Prefer-A §3 says "each shape-changing plan item (or Bound-documented equivalent)". Live `shapeChanging` is scope-level only; `collectSpecImpacts` OR-aggregates. The "or equivalent" clause can re-admit whole-scope soft discharge.
- **Failure mode:** Implement keeps scope OR under an "equivalent" gloss; one nested `delta` still clears uncovered siblings — P2 unrelieved while fixtures stay advise-green.
- **Disposition consequence:** Close the coverage unit in Prefer-A (examples that would bind: every `items`/`subItems` node under a shape-changing completion needs its own namespaced impact including explicit `none`; or leaf-only; or status=completed only). Drop unbounded "or equivalent" unless the equivalent is named in the same lean.

### F3 — blocks-the-design: enforce fail-closed at scope-complete contradicts the advise catch-all sync path

- **Evidence:** Prefer-A §1 names "scope-complete refuse or durable block". Sync hook swallows advise errors so lifecycle moves never fail closed. Enforcement enum is unread at the evaluator/writer.
- **Failure mode:** Bound claims refuse-on-complete while the only wired writer stays swallow → enforce is theater; or implement removes swallow without a closed limb and CI/agents disagree on whether `scope:complete` aborts, blocks durably, or only fails a later `verify:spec-drift`.
